title: Exact Resonances Are Not Sufficient for Phonon Energy Diffusion
authors: Wei Lin, Yong Zhang, Hong Zhao
abstract: Multi-phonon resonance conditions underpin kinetic theories of phonon transport and lattice thermalization. We show that exact resonance matching, nonzero interaction coefficients, and network connectivity do not guarantee persistent energy diffusion. Symmetry-enforced balance relations drive exact-resonant collision currents to nonthermal zero-flux states, producing kinetic arrest from individual resonant sets to connected networks. Complete energy spreading is sustained by quasi-resonances. The thermodynamic and weak-nonlinearity limits do not commute: the leading kinetic behavior is recovered in the former, whereas at fixed finite size the thermalization time diverges through higher-order crossovers as the nonlinearity vanishes. Exact-resonance existence and connectivity are therefore kinematic, not sufficient dynamical, criteria for phonon energy diffusion.
summary: The paper investigates phonon energy diffusion in anharmonic lattices, arguing that simple resonance matching is insufficient for achieving full thermalization. It demonstrates that symmetry constraints can cause kinetic arrest at non-thermal zero-flux states using only exact resonances. Complete energy spreading requires the inclusion of quasi-resonant interactions.
main_problem: The study challenges the assumption that merely establishing resonance matching and nonzero coupling is sufficient for persistent phonon energy diffusion (thermalization).
main_result: Exact resonances are only kinematic criteria, not sufficient dynamical ones; complete energy spreading requires quasi-resonances to overcome symmetry-enforced kinetic arrest.
method: The analysis uses theoretical derivations of kinetic equations and numerical simulations comparing the dynamics driven by exact versus quasi-resonant scattering processes.
model_or_system: The primary model is weakly anharmonic lattices, specifically using the periodic FPUT-6 lattice model. The system dynamics are governed by a derived kinetic equation from the sextic interaction term.
key_observables: Wave actions ($D_k$), normalized indicator entropy $\langle s(t) angle/(N-1)$, and relaxation times ($T_c$, $T_{eq}$).
important_parameters: Nonlinearity strength ($g$), system size ($N$), and the distinction between exact vs. quasi-resonance coupling widths ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between the thermodynamic limit and fixed finite sizes, noting that these limits do not commute.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows time evolution of wave actions for various resonance subsets leading to arrest; Figure 2 compares size dependence of coupling strengths for exact vs. quasi-resonances; Figure 3 illustrates energy evolution across different resonance regimes as nonlinearity decreases.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the conditions for phonon thermalization, first establishing the kinetic framework using FPUT models, then demonstrating that symmetry constraints cause arrest via exact resonances, and finally showing that quasi-resonances are necessary for full energy spreading.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical understanding of non-equilibrium dynamics in many-body systems, particularly highlighting how subtle spectral features (like the difference between exact vs. quasi-resonance) dictate whether a system reaches true thermal equilibrium or gets stuck in an arrested state.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Direct numerical verification of exact-resonant ki- netics in the periodic FPUT-6 chain. (a)–(e) Time evolution of the wave actions Dk for N = 32 and g = 10−2, retain- ing (a) a single symmetric sextet; (b) two coupled symmet- ric sextets; (c) all symmetric 3 ↔3 exact resonances; (d) all quasi-symmetric 3 ↔3 exact resonances; and (e) both families. (f) Normalized indicator entropy ⟨s(t)⟩/(N −1) for g = 10−2, 10−3, and 10−4. The solid and dashed lines corre- spond, respectively, to calculations retaining both resonance families and the symmetric family alone. The inset shows the relaxation time Tc, defined by ⟨s(Tc)⟩/(N −1) = 0.1; the dashed line indicates Tc ∝g−2.

FIG. 2. Size dependence of six-wave resonant channels. (a) Mode-averaged weighted connection strength ⟨p6(Ω)⟩as a function of the broadening width Ωfor N = 64, 128, 256, and 512. Solid curves show the quasi-resonant contribution from 0 < |∆ω| < Ω, whereas dashed horizontal lines show the exact-resonant contribution at ∆ω = 0. (b) Normalized indi- cator entropy ⟨s(t)⟩/(N −1) obtained from the exact-resonant kinetic equation including all allowed 3 ↔3 processes at g = 10−2 for the same system sizes.

FIG. 3. Full Hamiltonian dynamics of the periodic FPUT-6 chain. (a) Evolution of the k = ±1 mode energies for N=32, with g decreasing from 0.02 to 6 × 10−5. The horizontal lines mark the thresholds Ek=1 = 0.017 and Ek=1 = 0.007. (b) The same data plotted against the rescaled time g2t. (c) Relaxation time Tc as a function of g for the two thresholds in (a). (d) Equipartition time Teq for different system sizes. Dashed lines indicate reference power laws.

FIG. 4. Symmetry-constrained kinetic arrest in the DNLS model and the periodic FPUT-β chain. Exact four-wave ki- netic evolution of Dk for (a) the DNLS model and (b) the periodic FPUT-β chain, both with N = 32.

FIG. 5. Symmetry-constrained transient in the fixed- boundary FPUT-6 lattice. (a,b) Time evolution of the k = ±1 traveling-wave component energies for N = 32 and 64, re- spectively. The colored curves, from left to right, correspond to decreasing nonlinearity strengths from g = 3 × 10−3 to 10−4. As g decreases, the early-time dynamics increasingly approaches pairwise balance, followed by a slower redistribu- tion beyond the pairwise transient.
